title: A Google Calendar event references an issue or PR number that doesn't exist
author: esu-elegba
description: The Calendar-side twin of email-dangling-reference, and the twelfth leg of the dangling-reference family (after dangling-issue-reference, mention, release-note, issue-body, milestone-body, own-tweet, review-comment, issue-comment, linear-comment, slack-message, and email). calendar-event-claims-unfixed-issue's own docstring named this seam and deliberately left it open: 'a broken reference is a future calendar-side dangling-reference recipe's own seam, not this one's.' Extracts every bare #N reference (the shared seam_engine.references grammar every dangling-reference sibling already imports) from a calendar event's own title+description and checks it against BOTH the live issue list and the live PR list -- GitHub shares one number sequence between the two, so checking only one would misfire on a perfectly good reference to a merged PR. With this recipe, the google_calendar+github toolkit's own claims-X/dangling-reference grid names all three of the seams calendar-event-claims-dangling-milestone's own docstring left open (claims-dangling-milestone, task 1380; claims-open-milestone, task 1382; dangling-reference, here). Fixture-only, MOCK ONLY, never a live network call -- zero Google Calendar tools are exposed on the-hand gateway today, same WIP note all four existing Calendar recipes already carry. Neither ListIssues nor ListPullRequests is a new scope, and google_calendar+github is not a new toolkit pair.
confidence_notes: Flat 0.75, not age-gated -- email-dangling-reference's own exact score, not an independently re-reasoned number just because the reading surface is Calendar rather than Gmail: an organizer's own free text may simply be numbering a different tracker in their own head, the identical reasoning mention-dangling-reference's and email-dangling-reference's own docstrings already give for scoring below dangling-issue-reference's self-authored 0.8. A reference matching a real issue or PR is excluded at confidence 0.0, named not hidden -- the reference was simply good. An event with no #N reference at all produces no candidate whatsoever, not even an excluded one. Fixture-only (source: "fixture") per SCOPES.md's own WIP note on the Google Calendar toolkit: zero Calendar-capable tools are exposed on the-hand gateway's live toolset today -- the detection logic is real, the live read waits on the Hand's gateway, and only the fixture loaders swap for real calls the day they appear.
